name: Bhargavastra Counter Drone System

header.one_liner: Solar Defence Aerospace (SDAL) micro-missile hard-kill counter-swarm system under Indian Army Make-II; three firing trials completed May 2025, induction targeted end-2026.
header.maker: Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL) — system; Economic Explosives Limited (EEL) — munitions

what_it_is.prose: Bhargavastra is a multi-layer micro-missile and micro-rocket counter-swarm drone system designed and developed by Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL), a subsidiary of Solar Group / Solar Industries India Limited of Nagpur, with munitions (micro-rockets and micro-missiles) developed by Economic Explosives Limited, also a Solar Group company. The system is being developed under the Indian Army's Make-II programme (industry-funded prototype development). The system uses a layered defeat architecture: a first layer of unguided micro-rockets with a 20-metre lethal radius, and a second layer of guided micro-missiles with IIR/CCD guidance for hit-to-kill engagements. A single launcher carries 64 micro-rockets or micro-missiles in 8x8 cassettes, can salvo-fire the full load in under 10 seconds, and provides 360° coverage. Time from recognition to interception is under 16 seconds. Engagement range is up to 2.5 km. Detection is handled by a radar that identifies medium/large UAVs at 10 km, small drones at 6 km, and 0.01 m² RCS objects at greater than 5 km; an Electro-Optical Tracking System (EOTS) with 6 km range exceeds the Army's current 2.5 km operational requirement. The maiden firing occurred on 12 January 2025 at Gopalpur; three firing trials were conducted on 13 May 2025 at the Seaward Firing Range, Gopalpur, in the presence of senior Army Air Defence officials. The system was demonstrated to the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force at SDAL's Nagpur facility on 24-25 July 2026. SDAL Chairman Satyanarayan Nuwal stated on 24 July 2026 that internal trials would complete within 2-3 months, with induction targeted for end-2026. The Atlas register attributes this system to 'Big Bang Boom Solutions' — this attribution is contested by every credible 2025-26 source, which unanimously attribute Bhargavastra to SDAL. The conflict is documented in detail in open_questions below.

import_dependencies.summary: SDAL claims that 'every part — from strike mechanisms to detecting sensors — is developed in India'. No numerical indigenous content percentage has been disclosed. The solid propellant for the micro-rockets and micro-missiles is developed by Economic Explosives Limited (a Solar Group subsidiary) in India. The IIR/CCD seeker components, FPGA, and signal processing chain have not been publicly itemised by SDAL, so their origin remains an open question. Given industry-typical supply chains, FPGA and certain EO/IR components may be imported even when the system integrator is Indian.

faq.question: Who makes the Bhargavastra counter-drone system?
faq.answer: Per all credible 2025-26 sources — including The Economic Times, Times of India, The Hindu, ANI, Wikipedia, Bharat Shakti, Deccan Chronicle, Tribune, and Moneycontrol — Bhargavastra is designed and developed by Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL), a subsidiary of Solar Group / Solar Industries India Limited of Nagpur. The munitions (micro-rockets and micro-missiles) are developed by Economic Explosives Limited, also a Solar Group company. The Atlas register's attribution to 'Big Bang Boom Solutions' is contested and is the subject of an open data-conflict ticket.

faq.question: What is the Bhargavastra maker conflict?
faq.answer: The Atlas register lists the maker as 'Big Bang Boom Solutions' (BBBS, Chennai). All 2025-26 open sources — including primary interviews with SDAL Chairman Satyanarayan Nuwal — attribute Bhargavastra to Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL). BBBS's own counter-drone products are Vajra Sentinel and Vajra Shot; BBBS received an Indian MoD RFP in June 2022 for its Anti-Drone Defence System (ADDS) and signed a >₹200 crore MoD deal in March 2024 for Vajra Sentinel — none of which is Bhargavastra. The most plausible explanation is that the Atlas confused two distinct Indian counter-drone products during early data collection. The dossier treats SDAL as the authoritative maker and flags the conflict for Atlas correction.

faq.question: When will Bhargavastra be inducted?
faq.answer: SDAL Chairman Satyanarayan Nuwal stated on 24 July 2026 that internal trials would complete within 2-3 months (i.e., by approximately October 2026), with induction targeted for end-2026. The system is being developed under the Indian Army's Make-II programme (industry-funded prototype development).
